Theorem
[Solution of the transport initial-value problem]

↗ def:transport-explicit-solution

1. ch2:2.1.1-thm-1\group Transport Equation

If $g\in C^1(\R ^n)$, then $u(x,t)=g(x-tb)$ belongs to $C^1(\R ^n\times \R )$ and satisfies $u_t+b\cdot Du=0$.
Proof

\sketch Write $u=g\circ L$ for $L(x,t)=x-tb$. The transport operator is the directional derivative along $(b,1)$, and $L(b,1)=0$; the chain rule therefore gives $u_t+b\cdot Du=0$.

□
